The law must be designed to promote security of _powerful_ models, rather than, for example, models that might compromise individuals' privacy if stolen. If necessary, this will be decided by a judging panel made up of the Metaculus AI Forecasting team, or, failing that (e.g., because the AI Forecasting team no longer exists), at least 3 Metaculus admins: the judging panel would consider the stated intent of those who proposed the initial version of the bill.
question_details.fine_print: There may well be overlap between the most powerful models and the models that most compromise privacy. For this question’s resolution, what matters is whether the law is _intended_ to secure _powerful_ models.

In 2022, the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) released a draft amendment for public consultation. In March 2025, the CAC and relevant departments further developed a second draft for public comment. The first review of the draft amendment occurred at the 17th session of the 14th Standing Committee in September 2025. On October 23, 2025, Wang Xiang, spokesperson for the Legislative Affairs Commission of the NPC Standing Committee, reported that during the public consultation period from September 12 to October 11, 108 individuals submitted 162 comments. Based on feedback, the draft was revised to: (1) strengthen the guiding principles of cybersecurity work; (2) add provisions promoting AI safety and development; (3) improve alignment with the Civil Code and the Personal Information Protection Law in personal data protection; and (4) refine penalty provisions. The revised draft introduces a framework for AI safety and development, including support for foundational AI research, infrastructure advancement, ethical standards, risk monitoring, innovative security regulation, and healthy AI growth.
